title: DET Scoring: The 10–160 Scale & Subscores Explained
summary: How the Duolingo English Test builds your 10–160 overall from four skills, what the integrated subscores mean, and what universities check.

nodes.label: Overall
nodes.note: Average of the 4 skills, rounded to nearest 5

nodes.label: Check minimums
nodes.note: Universities may set overall AND subscore floors

chunks.heading: 10–160, built from four skills
chunks.body: Your **overall DET score runs 10–160 in 5-point steps** and is the **average of four Individual Subscores** — Reading, Writing, Speaking and Listening — **rounded to the nearest 5**. So each skill pulls the overall equally.
chunks.realExample: Reading 125, Writing 115, Speaking 110, Listening 120 → average 117.5 → overall rounds to about 120. One weak skill visibly drags the average, so balance pays.
chunks.memoryHook: Overall = average of the 4 skills, rounded to the nearest 5. Balance beats one spike.

chunks.heading: Integrated subscores — skills in pairs
chunks.body: Alongside the four skills, the DET reports **four Integrated Subscores**, each an average of two skills: **Literacy** (Reading + Writing), **Comprehension** (Reading + Listening), **Conversation** (Listening + Speaking) and **Production** (Speaking + Writing). Some programmes look at these.
chunks.realExample: A programme heavy on discussion might care about your Conversation subscore (Listening + Speaking); a research course might weigh Literacy (Reading + Writing). Know which pair your target values.
chunks.memoryHook: Four skills → four paired subscores: Literacy, Comprehension, Conversation, Production.

chunks.heading: Check the university's exact requirement
chunks.body: Universities set their own required DET score, and many list **both an overall minimum AND minimum subscores**. A strong overall with one weak skill can still miss a subscore floor — so read the **full requirement**, not just the headline number.
chunks.realExample: 'DET 120, no subscore below 105' means a 120 overall with a Writing of 100 would fall short. Always check for per-skill minimums before you decide you've met the bar.
chunks.memoryHook: Read the WHOLE requirement — overall AND any subscore minimums.

chunks.heading: Fast, and free to retake
chunks.body: DET **results arrive in about 48 hours**, and you can **take it again** (Duolingo allows multiple attempts, with limits per period) — so a below-target score isn't the end. Use your subscores to see exactly which skill to push before retaking.
chunks.realExample: If your overall is 5 points short and Speaking is your lowest subscore, focus practice there — lifting one weak skill is the fastest way to raise the average on a retake.
chunks.memoryHook: Results in ~48h; retakes allowed. Let your weakest subscore tell you what to fix.

recall.q: What is the DET overall score range and how is it calculated?
recall.a: 10–160 in 5-point steps; it's the average of the four skill subscores (Reading, Writing, Speaking, Listening), rounded to the nearest 5.

recall.q: What are the four integrated subscores and how are they formed?
recall.a: Literacy (Reading + Writing), Comprehension (Reading + Listening), Conversation (Listening + Speaking) and Production (Speaking + Writing) — each an average of two skills.

recall.q: Why check more than the overall score requirement?
recall.a: Many universities set both an overall minimum and minimum subscores, so a strong overall with one weak skill can still miss a subscore floor.

recall.q: How quickly do DET results arrive?
How should you use subscores before a retake?
recall.a: Identify your weakest skill subscore and focus practice there, since lifting one weak skill raises the overall average fastest.
